claude.rationale: The deal is a double reverse-triangular merger in which both predecessors became wholly owned operating subsidiaries of a newly formed top holding company (New Cigna, renamed Cigna), so each company's product/customer-facing business (T4) crossed together with its operational functions (T5): Cigna's operational functions stayed in Bloomfield and Express Scripts' "principal executive offices and related corporate and operational functions" remained in St. Louis under the Express Scripts division, showing product and processes moving together rather than a T4-vs-T5 split (gap_45=0). Likewise the operational processes remained coherently attached to their organization/people — Express Scripts' operations, its former CEO (now division President reporting to Cigna's CEO), and its St. Louis workforce stayed in place — so T5 was not re-engineered apart from the people/culture that run it (gap_56=0). T1 is coded replace because Cigna installed New Cigna's officers as its own and held nine of fourteen board seats plus 64% ownership, subordinating the Express Scripts CEO, indicating a dominant controlling intent rather than a fused merger-of-equals; T3 is swap given the new top holding-company domicile taking the Cigna name and NYSE listing.
